newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CBO sees FY97 budget deficit at $124 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CBO sees FY97 budget deficit at $124 bln.

text.p: The U.S. Congressional Budget Office estimated the fiscal 1997 budget deficit would be $124 billion if there were no policy changes, a much rosier forecast than the $171 billion deficit predicted last May, according to CBO figures made available to Congress Monday.
The CBO forecast the budget deficit would increase to $188 billion in 2002, a much lower projection than the $285 billion predicted last May.
CBO estimated fiscal 1997 revenues would be $1.51 trillion and increase to $1.86 trillion in fiscal 2002. Fiscal 1997 spending was forecast to be $1.6 trillion and increase to $2.0 trillion in 2002.
If Congress reaches agreement on a balanced budget, the CBO forecast deficit reduction of $154 billion would be needed in 2002.
That forecast gives Congress a bonus of $34 billion, called the "fiscal dividend," for an expected boost to the economy resulting from an agreement.
CBO previously had estimated $210 billion deficit reduction would be needed for 2002 if there were a balanced budget agreement.

President Clinton is scheduled to release his budget Feb. 6. The last budget deficit estimate from the White House Office of Management and Budget for fiscal 2002 was $109 billion, assuming no changes in law, released last March.
